key_insight: A physics-informed variational autoencoder with a Gaussian copula can estimate bridge damage while explicitly modeling uncertainty and structural physics.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support earlier, more reliable damage screening in bridge monitoring by reducing false confidence from noisy vibration data.
method: Embed a differentiable numerical eigenvalue solver inside the VAE to enforce structural dynamics.
Use a Gaussian copula latent model to capture correlated, physics-dependent damage patterns.
Train and test on simulated bridge vibration data with stochastic Gaussian noise.
evidence_signal: On a synthetic simply supported bridge dataset with ground-truth stiffness values, the method achieved 77.2% posterior coverage.
watch_item: Because validation was performed on synthetic data, real-world performance may differ under sensor placement limits, model mismatch, and changing environmental conditions.
paper_title: Uncertainty-aware damage identification in short-span bridges via physics-informed variational autoencoder
